question: Following a letter of reply from the Commission to EUROMIL, issues were raised concerning the provision of air navigation services at the military airbase of Aktion, which serves an increasing number of civilian flights.

According to relevant information, the military air navigation service provider has not been certified by the competent Civil Aviation Authority and the European Union Aviation Safety Agency is apparently aware of this.

However, Regulations (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2017/373 provide for obligations with regard to certification, oversight, adequate staffing and ensuring a high level of safety for providers serving general air traffic. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Is it aware of the above?
Is all the above in line with existing EU law?

Does it intend to take measures vis-à-vis the competent Greek authorities to ensure the full implementation of the above regulations and of any other legislation applicable in this case, at military airbases serving civil air traffic?
answer: As rightly stated by the Honourable Member, questions related to certification of aerodromes are under the responsibility and oversight of the Greek Competent Authority.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) in turn oversees the National Competent Authority after which, if non-compliance with EU law is detected and not being resolved, the Commission is formally notified by EASA and could raise a formal infringement procedure. To date, the Commission has not been notified by EASA to this end.

The Commission underlines the importance of ensuring the safety of operations of military aerodromes handling civil traffic in accordance with Article 2.5 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (EASA) (1) and Article 7.4 of Regulation (EU) 2024/2803 (Single European Sky) (2), where applicable.
